findings.description: Requirement 3 (the two read differently) holds: applying the convergent test, each pair splits on "<tool> not found — skipping" versus "<tool> ran, but could not", so a reader seeing one line alone can name the case without an exit code.
findings.evidence:
Skip vs failure, per site, quoted from the executed runs:
  packages: "Homebrew not found — skipping package install."        | "Homebrew ran, but could not install these Brewfile entries..."
  vscode:   "VS Code CLI not found — skipping extension install."   | "VS Code ran, but could not install these extensions..."
  claude:   "claude CLI not found — skipping plugin install."       | "The claude CLI ran, but these did not install..."
  raycast:  "open command not found — skipping Raycast configuration." | "macOS would not hand these install URLs to Raycast..."
Neither side borrows the other's phrasing: "skipping" appears in no failure line, "ran, but could not"/"would not hand" in no skip line.

findings.description: Requirement 5 (the reason survives) holds: no `2>/dev/null` remains on any install call whose failure the script reports, and each failing tool's stderr reached the run's output alongside the named item.
findings.evidence:
$ grep -n '2>/dev/null' on each converted template — only three occurrences survive, none on a reported install call:
  run_onchange_install-packages.sh.tmpl:27  brew trust --tap "$tap" 2>/dev/null || true            (tap pre-trust, not an install; B-1 permits it)
  run_onchange_after_install-claude-plugins.sh.tmpl:39  claude plugin marketplace list 2>/dev/null | grep -q  (presence probe; its failure is never reported)
  run_onchange_after_install-claude-plugins.sh.tmpl:48  claude plugin list 2>/dev/null | grep -q               (presence probe; same)
  run_onchange_install-vscode-extensions.sh.tmpl:19 is the string inside a comment, not code.
Measured stderr survival — each failing stub's message appeared on the run's stderr:
  vscode:  "STUBERR: extension 'dbaeumer.vscode-eslint' not found in marketplace"
  raycast: "STUBERR: LSOpenURLsWithRole() failed for raycast://extensions/install/brew"
  claude:  "STUBERR: repository 'kendrick/agent-guild' not found"
  packages: brew's own output stays on screen via `tee` (run_onchange_install-packages.sh.tmpl:41)

findings.description: Each multi-call site collects and reports once at the end, continuation is preserved, and no script could be made to exit non-zero in any of the eleven scenarios executed — including a total-failure run at every site.
findings.evidence:
Single end-of-run summary per site, confirmed by output shape above; per-item chatter is only the attempt trace, never a per-item verdict.
Continuation and exit status, worst case at each multi-call site:
  vscode, every extension failing  -> 43 code invocations logged, 43 ids named, EXIT=0
  raycast, every URL refused AND `defaults` stubbed to rc=1 -> 27 open invocations logged, 27 URLs named, EXIT=0
  claude, all 7 calls failing -> 7 invocations logged, all 7 named (3 marketplaces + 4 plugins), EXIT=0
packages is exempt (one `brew bundle`) and still names entries; it also exits 0 on an unrecognised brew failure shape:
  "Homebrew ran and exited 1 without naming a failed entry. Its output is above."  EXIT=0
Static sweep for a non-zero exit path across all four templates: grep -nE 'exit [1-9]' returns nothing; every script ends `exit 0`.
The orchestrator-flagged path specifically: `defaults` stubbed to fail with one URL refused still printed "Could not set Raycast's global hotkey; its preferences are unchanged." followed by the refused-URL summary, EXIT=0. run_onchange_configure-raycast.sh.tmpl:46-48 consumes the status with `if !` rather than letting `set -e` abort before the summary.

findings.description: The raycast site claims only what it can observe: it reports `open` refusing a URL and never a per-extension install outcome, and a comment records why it can go no further.
findings.evidence:
run_onchange_configure-raycast.sh.tmpl:21-25 records the ceiling: "`open` hands the URL to launchd and returns the moment macOS accepts it, well before Raycast has fetched, built, or rejected anything — so a per-extension install outcome is not merely unchecked here, it is unobservable."
Every line the script can print, checked against B-4:
  :19 "Requesting Raycast extension installs..." — a request, not an outcome
  :31 "  → $ext" — attempt trace
  :53 "macOS would not hand these install URLs to Raycast" — a handoff refusal, which is exactly what B-2 requirement 2 scopes this site to
  :56 "Raycast install requests sent. Raycast picks them up in the background." — explicitly disclaims the outcome
No line resembling B-4's failing example ("Installed 12 Raycast extensions.") exists. The one other outcome the script names, :47 "Could not set Raycast's global hotkey; its preferences are unchanged.", is a `defaults write` result — synchronous and directly observable, and not an extension install outcome — so it is outside what B-4 forbids.

findings.description: bash 3.2 safety holds: every array expansion sits inside its own count guard, and no associative array, `${var^^}`, or `set -u` appears.
findings.evidence:
$ grep -n '\[@\]' on the four templates — six hits, three count tests and three expansions, each expansion immediately inside its own guard:
  run_onchange_install-vscode-extensions.sh.tmpl:38  if [ "${#failed[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  run_onchange_install-vscode-extensions.sh.tmpl:40    printf '  %s\n' "${failed[@]}"
  run_onchange_configure-raycast.sh.tmpl:52  if [ "${#refused[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  run_onchange_configure-raycast.sh.tmpl:54    printf '  raycast://extensions/install/%s\n' "${refused[@]}"
  run_onchange_after_install-claude-plugins.sh.tmpl:95  if [ "${#failed[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  run_onchange_after_install-claude-plugins.sh.tmpl:97    printf '  %s\n' "${failed[@]}"
$ grep -nE 'exit [1-9]|set -u|declare -A|\$\{[A-Za-z_]+\^\^' on all four -> (none)
The empty-accumulator path was executed rather than inferred: all four clean runs under GNU bash 3.2.57(1)-release printed 0 blank lines, so the defect B-5's failing example describes does not occur.
No accumulator leans on errexit through `|| true`; each uses `if ! <cmd>; then arr+=(...); fi`. `install-packages` uses `${PIPESTATUS[0]}` (:42) rather than `$?` through the `tee`, and it correctly carried brew's exit 1 in the measured failure run.

findings.description: Every added comment carries information the code cannot: the incident, the tool's output format, a bash 3.2 constraint, or the reason a reader must not "fix" the exit status. None is deletable without loss.
findings.evidence:
Reviewed all eighteen added/amended comment blocks in `git diff` of the four templates. Representative load-bearing ones:
  install-packages:32-33 records the incident the job exists for — "on 2026-08-06 fzf joined the core bundle, brew never installed it, and the run said the same thing it says on a machine that is merely waiting on an App Store password."
  install-packages:40 preempts the exact footgun in the line below it — "PIPESTATUS[0] is brew's status; $? would be tee's, always 0."
  install-packages:45-49 documents brew's output format, the SGR wrapping, and why the count line is deliberately excluded — none of which the awk can state itself.
  configure-raycast:41-45 explains why `defaults write` is wrapped: under `set -e` it "used to abort the script right here — exiting non-zero over a preference and taking the list of refused URLs down with it." I reproduced exactly that failure path and confirmed the wrap is what prevents it.
  install-claude-plugins:37-38 explains why two `2>/dev/null` survive: "survives on the probe, not on the install: `marketplace list` grumbles on a machine that has none registered yet."
  install-claude-plugins:28-30 explains why the accumulator is global rather than function-local: "a flat run of add_marketplace and install_plugin calls rather than a loop, so the accumulator lives out here where both functions can reach it."
  Each of the three `exit 0` comments guards against the misreading the issue title invites, e.g. install-packages:72-73 "Stopping the apply here would strand every later script over one unavailable formula."
The three near-duplicate bash 3.2 empty-array comments (vscode:35-37, raycast:50-51, claude:93-94) are not redundant within any single file, which is where a reader encounters them. Register matches the existing headers (e.g. install-packages:3-5). The one what-style comment in range, configure-raycast:29 "# Skip comments and empty lines", is pre-existing context in the diff, not added by this task.
